idiom_name: values.filter((v): v is T => ...) (copy) or write-index compaction + length truncation
implementation_notes: Same runtime as JavaScript plus one genuinely typed realisation: filter accepts a user-defined type predicate, so removing the elements that fail a test can narrow the survivor array's element type - values.filter((v): v is Row => v !== null) turns (Row | null)[] into Row[] in one pass, and the compiler checks that the predicate really is a test for Row. That form is copy-out (a new array while the original still holds the rejected members), which is usually what a TypeScript codebase wants because it converts an inconvenient union into a clean type. When the array must keep its identity, the in-place form is the same untyped write-index compaction as in JavaScript followed by arr.length = n, and the type system does not narrow it: narrowing exists only on the new value. readonly T[] forbids splice and push at compile time, but a mutable alias of the same array still mutates it, so immutability must be enforced by types rather than assumed.
pitfalls: A type predicate is trusted, not verified: a wrong guard makes the narrowed type lie, and narrowing applies to the new array only - the original array still holds the removed members.
The in-place compaction carries no narrowing at all: after arr.length = n the compiler still believes the old element union, so a second pass needs a separate filter, a cast, or a re-typed view.

readonly T[] and ReadonlyArray reject splice/push at compile time, but assigning a mutable array to a readonly reference does not make it immutable; and no index read after a truncation is bounds-checked at runtime.
sources: MDN, Array.prototype.filter() - creates a shallow copy containing the elements that pass the test, and the callback is not invoked for holes: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/filter

TypeScript Handbook, Narrowing - 'Using type predicates' documents the (x): x is T form that makes filter narrow the result's element type: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/narrowing.html
